$comment: Turkish housing loan rules. Pinned rather than looked up at runtime, and every rule carries where it came from, when it was captured, and whether it was read in a primary source. Most tables on the open web still show the 2023 decision and are wrong.

loan_to_value.note: Ratio of the loan to the APPRAISED value of the housing taken as collateral — not the asking price. Madde 12(1) requires a licensed valuation and requires that figure to be the base. The 29.01.2026 decision removed the new/second-hand distinction; the ratio now depends only on value and energy class, and carries no absolute ceiling.

energy_classes.A_B: A or B on the Enerji Kimlik Belgesi (Law 5627)

source.still_in_force_per: Kurul Kararı 11364 (29.01.2026), which applies it to the new ratios

existing_home_reduction.note: If the borrower, their spouse, or a child under 18 already owns at least one home, the ratio above is reduced by 75% — a quarter of it applies. The single largest effect in this file. Not counted as ownership: homes in villages and in places that became neighbourhoods under Law 6360; a share of 50% or less in one home's title, unless there are shares in more than one; and a sole home demolished or condemned as riskli yapı under Law 6306 (Kurul Kararı 10849, 15.02.2024).

source.checked: Bankaların Kredi İşlemlerine İlişkin Yönetmelik madde 12, and all 20 Kurul Kararları attached to it between 19.03.2020 and 29.01.2026

term.note: There is NO legal maximum maturity for a housing loan. Madde 12(3) sets one for consumer loans and excludes konut edinme kredileri from it by name; no Kurul Kararı sets one for housing. The figure below is what banks commonly offer, kept as a default, and must never be presented as a legal limit. The consumer-loan limits (36/24/12 months by size, Kurul Kararı 11152) are a different product and are routinely confused with this one.
term.age_note: Also practice rather than regulation. BDDK's Kredi Tahsis ve İzleme Rehberi leaves customer age limits and maximum maturities to each bank, and reasons from expected retirement age rather than a fixed 70.

bsmv_source.authority: Law 5582 madde 30, amending Gider Vergileri Kanunu (6802) madde 29/(y)

kkdf_source.authority: Bakanlar Kurulu Kararı 88/12944 and its rate schedule, which carves out loans made for the purchase of real estate
kkdf_source.note: Correct in practice but not read in a primary source — mevzuat.gov.tr, resmigazete.gov.tr and gib.gov.tr were all unreachable. NOT from Law 5582: that law contains no KKDF provision, and an earlier version of this file attributed it there wrongly.

taxes.note: The two exemptions turn on different tests, which is the trap. BSMV follows whether the transaction is konut finansmanı as defined in 6362 SPKn madde 57, which includes borrowing against a home already owned. KKDF follows whether the loan is FOR THE PURCHASE of real estate. So a konut-teminatlı ihtiyaç kredisi is BSMV-exempt but KKDF-liable, and treating housing collateral as implying both are zero understates its cost.
